chunks: 2575 - And in the narration of Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār, from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
"You garland it with an old sandal in which you have prayed, and al-ish'ār and al-taqlīd are in the position of the talbiyah."

key_terms.التَّقْلِيدُ: garlanding the sacrificial animal as a ritual sign
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the formal pilgrim invocation whose legal role is paralleled here
key_terms.الْإِشْعَارُ: marking the sacrificial animal as part of the hajj rite
key_terms.تُقَلِّدُهَا: you garland it, meaning to place a sign on the sacrificial animal
key_terms.نَعْلًا خَلَقًا: an old sandal, used here as the item for garlanding

ai.seo_question: How should a sacrificial animal be garlanded and what is the status of ish'ar and taqlid in relation to talbiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction regarding the designation of sacrificial animals in hajj rites. It states that garlanding the animal with an old sandal used in prayer, along with marking and garlanding, carries the legal status of talbiyah in this ritual context.
